newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo 1996 inflation seen to head for 10-yr low.
newsitem.headline: Yugo 1996 inflation seen to head for 10-yr low.

text.p: Yugoslavia's 1996 inflation, measured by the retail price index (RPI), will fall below 60 percent to the lowest level in 10 years, the federal statistics office said on Wednesday.
"In December 1996 inflation will range between 50 and 60 percent year-on-year," assistant general manager of the Yugoslav Statistics Office Mirjana Rankovic told a news conference.
November RPI will include lower meat prices if the trend continues, she added.
"Over the last week of October there was a sporadic reduction in meat prices. If it continues, it will be included in the November RPI," Rankovic said.
October retail prices grew 1.4 percent on September. They were 69.6 percent up on October 1995. Cummulative ten-month inflation stood at 49.2 percent on December 1995.
September inflation was 1.2 percent month-on-month, or 83.8 percent year-on-year.
October saw an overall stabilisation of retail prices, both of goods and services, with the latter rising only symbolically by 0.2 percent, Rankovic said.
Services sector was blamed for a high 6.6 percent monthly inflation in July.
